subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious. One novel; all fixated on Obsession.

novels.title: Bloom
novels.author: Delilah S. Dawson (2023)
novels.vibe: A cottagecore sapphic romance that curdles into body horror once the farmer's-market girlfriend turns out to be something else entirely.
novels.summary: Ro falls hard and fast for Ash, a charming stranger she meets at the local farmer's market, swept up in a whirlwind of homemade jam and infatuation. As the relationship intensifies, the story pulls back the curtain on what Ash really is and what she wants from Ro, turning cozy romance into claustrophobic body horror.
novels.warnings: Body horror, past child abuse, animal cruelty, abusive guardian (past), abandonment, disordered eating themes.

novels.title: Brother
novels.author: Ania Ahlborn (2015)
novels.vibe: A brutal Appalachian family-of-killers novel about a teenager trying to break away from what his family does in the woods.
novels.summary: Michael grows up in an isolated Appalachian farmhouse where his family's disturbing traditions have gone unnoticed by the outside world for years. As girls keep disappearing off the nearby highway, Michael is forced to reckon with what his family truly is, and whether he can escape it.
novels.warnings: Extreme violence and gore, torture, incest, child abuse, animal cruelty/death, cannibalism, kidnapping, misogyny.

novels.title: Misery
novels.author: Stephen King (1987)
novels.vibe: The definitive captor-and-captive horror novel — a writer at the mercy of his "number one fan" after a car crash.
novels.summary: After a near-fatal car accident, novelist Paul Sheldon wakes up in the care of former nurse Annie Wilkes, his self-proclaimed biggest fan, in her remote home. When Annie discovers Paul has killed off her favorite character, her devotion turns into escalating, sadistic captivity.
novels.warnings: Graphic torture (including amputation), confinement, addiction, substance abuse, violence, psychological abuse.

novels.title: Cabal
novels.author: Clive Barker (1988)
novels.vibe: A monstrous found-family horror novella where the real killers turn out to be entirely human.
novels.summary: Boone, convinced by his manipulative therapist that he's a serial killer, turns himself in and learns of Midian, a hidden refuge for shape-shifting creatures called the Nightbreed. As Boone is drawn into Midian and its inhabitants, the story flips expectations about who the real monsters are, building to a bloody confrontation with the humans hunting the Nightbreed down.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and gore, body horror, mass murder, psychological manipulation, mob violence.

short_works.title: Things Have Gotten Worse Since We Last Spoke
short_works.author: Eric LaRocca (2021)
short_works.vibe: A viral, deeply disturbing epistolary novella about an online relationship that spirals into escalating psychological and physical horror.
short_works.summary: Told through emails and chat logs, the story follows Agnes and Zoe's online relationship after Agnes buys a strange antique apple peeler from Zoe. What begins as flirtation curdles into an increasingly extreme, mutually consuming psychological and physical descent.
short_works.warnings: Extreme body horror and self-harm, graphic sexual content, psychological manipulation and abuse, animal death, suicide.

short_works.title: The Monster of Elendhaven
short_works.author: Jennifer Giesbrecht (2019)
short_works.vibe: A grim, atmospheric novella about a plague-scarred port city, a nameless killer, and the sickly sorcerer who takes him in.
short_works.summary: In the decaying, plague-ravaged city of Elendhaven, a mysterious and nearly unkillable man becomes the tool of a bitter, ailing sorcerer bent on revenge against the city's elite. Their dark partnership escalates into a violent, intimate horror story about power, obsession, and rot.
short_works.warnings: Extreme graphic violence, gore, body horror, murder, disease/plague themes.
